newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia plans to privatise 63 firms by end-1997.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia plans to privatise 63 firms by end-1997.

text.p: Tunisia plans to privatise 63 public firms by the end of 1997, including cement companies and stakes in the national airline Tunis Air and the oil distribution company Societe Nationale de Distribution des Petroles (SNDP), a senior Tunisian official said on Thursday.

"We have earmarked for privatisation 63 firms representing about $1.4 billion assets," Moncef Ben Abdallah, Secretary of State to the Ministry of Economic Development in charge of privatisations told a meeting of the Tunisian-American Chamber of Commerce.
"We are in the process of launching some 30 of them representing a total assets of $30 million, and the remaining will be launched within 12 months," he added.
"By mid-1997, we aim at having privatised 50 percent of the 63 firms' assets, including cement companies," Ben Abdallah said.
He said the privatisation candidates also included firms in the food, textiles, pharmaceuticals and chemical sectors.
"We intend to privatise partially some firms by opening up their capital through the stock exchange. We are preparing a new public offer of Tunis Air shares for the next months," Ben Abdallah said.

"We are also preparing an opening up of the capital of SNDP, and of some trading firms such as retail stores Magasin General and real estate company SIMPAR. These offers are already ready and will be launched soon," he added.

"There is no limitation for foreigners to buy Tunisian privatised firms. The only one is on the stock exchange where they can purchase without prior authorisation up to 10 percent of a listed firm's capital, and up to 30 percent of non-listed firms," Ben Abdallah said.
He said that 77 small and medium public firms had been privatised so far since 1989.
"The new stage is that of the privatisation of biggest firms...This requires more transparency for which we will need the help of merchant banks for their evaluation," he said.

There is only one merchant bank in Tunisia's financial sector, International Maghreb Merchant Bank, set up last year with the support of the World Bank's International Finance corporation (IFC). ($=0.98 dinar)
